Subject: Sundial Health — KV-caching & topology deep-dive (post-call)

Thanks again for the time this morning — appreciate the candid discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps from Redwood: 

High-level pain & goals (captured on call):
- Primary pain: user-facing latency spikes during batch report generation (90th pct spikes from 220ms to 1.2s under load).
- Secondary: unpredictable token cost on long multi-turn summaries; need for predictable per-call pricing for finance.
- Goal: 95th pct latency target <= 300ms for single-request flows; 99th pct <= 500ms for low-vol queries. For heavy batch jobs (async), throughput target ~600 reqs/min with tail-latency < 1s.

Technical constraints (your inputs):
- Model: T5-based family for structured summaries; looking at 7B–13B open models with int8 quantization.
- KV reuse expected: high token-prefix overlap across repeat report generations — good candidate for prefix/KV caching.
- Network: VPC peering required for PHI-proximal services; data residency US-only.
- Ops: Sundial prefers Reserved/Dedicated capacity for predictable billing and isolation, but open to hybrid for peaks.

Redwood proposal (initial):
1) Topology: Dedicated GPU pool in us-west with a small hosted fallback cluster in us-east for overflow. VPC peering + private endpoints for control plane.
2) Model & quant: Recommend 13B int8 quantized variant as baseline; experiment with 7B quant for batch-heavy workloads.
3) KV caching: deploy per-customer KV shard with prefix caching and adaptive TTL; expect 30–45% token cost reduction on repeat sequences.
4) SLOs & routing: route latency-sensitive routes to low-burst dedicated pool; batch jobs to autoscaled burst nodes with lower priority.

Requested next steps (action items):
- Sundial: share sample production trace (1 hour) and a small sample of the prompt corpus (anonymized) — to size cache hit expectations.
- Sundial: review attached capacity matrix; fill in expected QPS and peak concurrency.
- Redwood: we will run a quick fit analysis and share a topology sketch + preliminary cost delta within 48 hours.

Attachments: sundial_capacity_matrix_v2.xlsx, topology_sketch.drawio

Best,
Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Hey Samir — got the ask on routing/budgets. A few operational details and a short technical sketch so you have something concrete to share with your infra team: 

Operational knobs we’ll use:
- Per-route token caps: yes — can enforce max_tokens per request plus dynamic guardrails based on rolling cost budget. We surface token-usage per-call in the Console.
- KV cache design: per-customer in-memory shards colocated with serving nodes. Cache key = (model-version, prompt-prefix-hash). TTL is tunable; we recommend conservative 6-hour warm window for report-style reuse, with metrics to monitor hit-rate.
- Fallbacks: when cache miss + high latency, autoscaling policy allows routing to fallback hosted pool (longer cold-start) or to a lower-precision model for burst traffic.

Latency/Throughput Sizing (initial assumptions using your sample traces):
- Target workload: 420 concurrent peak, median prompt length 320 tokens, median response 120 tokens.
- Model perf: 13B int8 => ~18ms/token on A100-class serving; 7B int8 => ~9ms/token.
- Cache hit improvement: for prefixes with 70% reuse expected, per-request token compute reduces by ~45%.
- Estimated tail: with KV caching + dedicated pool we expect 95th pct <= 260ms for single interactive calls; 99th pct ~420–480ms depending on I/O.

Topology recommendation (sketch):
1) Customer-dedicated pool (us-west) — N nodes (we’ll right-size after you fill the capacity matrix). Nodes run the quantized 13B variant, with KV shards.
2) Overflow hosted fleet (us-east) — lower-cost preemptible nodes for batch jobs; integrated routing by policy.
3) Private control-plane endpoints via VPC peering (mutual TLS) to satisfy compliance.

Low-risk POC plan (2–3 weeks):
- Week 0: share traces + capacity matrix (you).
- Week 1: Redwood builds small dedicated pool (2–4 GPUs) and runs synthetic replay of your trace.
- Week 2: Adjust cache TTLs, measure hit-rate, iterate model quant settings; present fit analysis and cost delta.

Attachments: topology_sketch.drawio

If this aligns, we can schedule the infra-level kickoff. I’m looping Karthik to run sizing.

—Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
